scope: Read-only primary-source review of pi0.5 deployment, ONNX/TensorRT, mixed INT4 and JAX unified memory. No GPU execution, environment installation or robot action was performed by this research task.

project_evidence_update.receipt_summary: Lead agent verified a new receipt reporting original checkpoint 9999 running on RTX 3060 Laptop GPU 6 GiB with runtime='Orbax/JAX unified memory, restore_concurrent_gb=3'; log describes typical inference around 0.4-0.5 s.
project_evidence_update.evidence_boundary: This research task did not independently execute or profile that run. Treat the receipt as project evidence, not a general benchmark or proof of physical all-GPU residency.
project_evidence_update.revised_recommendation: Preserve the already successful local JAX unified-memory path for the first real test. ONNX and mixed INT4 are optional optimization branches; remote OpenPI serving remains an available fallback rather than a prerequisite.
project_evidence_update.supersedes: The earlier recommendation to use remote inference first was made before the new local-success receipt became available.

model_contract.preprocessing: Preserve project RGB resize/padding and pixel convention, prompt/state tokenization, and original train-set quantile normalization.
model_contract.postprocessing: Restore six arm-joint deltas to absolute targets exactly once using the observation state; keep the gripper action absolute. Generic third-party unnormalization/slicing is not a replacement.
model_contract.timing: A 20 Hz data grid and ten predicted steps imply a nominal 0.5 s action horizon; they do not establish 20 Hz policy replanning or actual closed-loop latency.

weight_storage_arithmetic.definition: N * bits / 8, ideal weight storage only; excludes mixed-precision exceptions, scales/zero-points, activations, KV cache, temporary buffers and backend workspace.
weight_storage_arithmetic.interpretation: 6.246 GiB excludes a simple all-weights-resident 16-bit allocation within 6 GiB, but does not exclude unified-memory oversubscription, CPU offload, streaming or component residency. ONNX serialization alone does not provide quantization or offload. Mixed INT4 runtime memory cannot be inferred from the all-INT4 ideal.

jax_unified_memory.actual_installed_version: Must be taken from the successful field environment; current upstream source is explanatory evidence and is not proof of the installed build.
findings: OpenXLA's GPU BFC allocator reads TF_FORCE_UNIFIED_MEMORY and selects MemorySpace::kUnified when enabled.

In the inspected source, the unified-memory allocator budget is total physical device memory multiplied by max(1.0, start_fraction); the code explicitly permits memory_fraction > 1 for oversubscription.

On supported CUDA systems, managed allocations may exceed physical GPU memory and migrate between host and device. A larger virtual allocation therefore does not imply all weights reside in VRAM simultaneously.
Disabling JAX preallocation alone does not enable host spill. The allocation mode, unified-memory flag and memory-fraction settings have distinct roles.

The latest JAX docs use XLA_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION and describe XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION as a deprecated alias. Capture whichever variables the installed successful environment actually uses; do not replace working settings with upstream defaults.
Do not infer the field run's exact page residency, host-memory cost, migration pattern or speed penalty from the receipt label alone.

sources.purpose: Preallocation, memory-fraction and allocator meanings; version-sensitive defaults.
Managed-memory migration and oversubscription; support depends on platform and device capabilities.
Official JAX application example of unified memory using TF_FORCE_UNIFIED_MEMORY, preallocation=false and memory fraction > 1. This is not a pi0.5-specific recommended parameter set.

orbax_restore.meaning: restore_concurrent_gb limits how many checkpoint bytes may be restored concurrently. It reduces concurrent restore pressure; it is not final-model memory, a runtime VRAM cap, compression, or a change in policy precision.
orbax_restore.units_in_inspected_source: _concurrent_bytes multiplies the setting by 10**9; 3 means 3,000,000,000 bytes, not 3 GiB.
orbax_restore.implementation: PyTreeCheckpointHandler converts the setting to bytes and passes it to BasePyTreeCheckpointHandler; the latter creates a shared byte limiter for deserialization.
orbax_restore.cautions: The process must still hold restored model arrays and other buffers; total RAM/VRAM can exceed the configured concurrent restore amount. Confirm the installed Orbax version and actual handler invocation.

field_receipt_to_preserve.purpose: Collect these facts during the existing actual inference/control task and retain the successful launch recipe; no separate capacity-test project is implied.
launch: Exact command, working directory, environment entry point and checkpoint 9999 path/hash.

Only relevant environment variables: TF_FORCE_UNIFIED_MEMORY, XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_PREALLOCATE, XLA_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION, XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION, XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_ALLOCATOR, TF_GPU_ALLOCATOR, XLA_FLAGS, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES, JAX_PLATFORMS and compilation-cache settings. Preserve unset versus set values; do not dump unrelated secrets.
Actual restore_concurrent_gb setting and source change or constructor call that applies it.
Python, jax, jaxlib, CUDA plugin/PJRT and orbax-checkpoint versions; CUDA driver, OS/kernel, exact GPU name and memory total.
Runtime JAX device/backend, model config, inference denoising steps, loaded dtype distribution, original norm/assets hashes and input preprocessing.
memory: Available system RAM and swap before launch; process RSS/high-water mark and system available RAM during restore, first compile/warmup and ongoing inference.
GPU memory used/peak during those same phases, including display and other-process usage.
Loaded array byte accounting and dtype distribution may describe virtual logical storage, not physical CUDA-managed page residency.
If exact spill behavior is claimed later, retain an actual relevant trace; do not infer it from nvidia-smi alone.
latency: Keep cold restore/compile separate from warmed inference; retain sample count, median/P95/max and input shape.

A JAX call can return before device work finishes. Time through block_until_ready or host materialization of the action array; service response timing may already synchronize but must be verified from the actual code.
For the robot, retain observation capture/receive time, policy completion, target dispatch and execution timing. Distinguish policy duration from complete observation-to-action age.
The reported typical 0.4-0.5 s is not yet a P95, a worst-case guarantee, a 20 Hz policy rate or proof of full task success.

findings: Official README reference inference requirement is >8 GB; this is a documented reference requirement rather than an impossibility theorem for every offload configuration.
Official PyTorch support and JAX-to-PyTorch conversion are available; remote WebSocket serving is documented.
The inspected converter advertises float16 in its type annotation but its dtype branch only accepts float32 and bfloat16. Do not prescribe --precision float16 with this commit.
Use the project's actual model config and assets rather than a stock DROID config.

phyai_mixed_int4.evidence_level: Original implementation and presets inspected; no RTX 3060 Laptop 6 GiB run or this custom checkpoint evaluation was established.
findings: The Humming W4A16 preset targets NVIDIA SM80+ and applies load-time symmetric RTN INT4 weight quantization with block shape [1,128] to language/action-expert attention and MLP linear projections.
Vision, token embeddings, action/time heads and norms remain at higher precision. Activations remain BF16/FP16. This is mixed precision, not an all-weights INT4 model.
PI05Config defaults chunk_size to 50 and discards unknown configuration keys. Blindly reading OpenPI's action_horizon=10 does not set chunk_size=10; map this explicitly.
The processor's output path unnormalizes, slices actions and moves to CPU. It does not implement this project's six-joint AbsoluteActions restoration.
Without the correct dataset statistics, generic normalization may be identity. Preserve this project's own quantiles, state-tokenization and pixel convention.
The example script can use random observations; that does not validate the trained Piper policy.
Explicit noise is supported by the request path, permitting reproducible action comparison on the real held-out observations.
phyai_mixed_int4.next_use: Only if optimizing beyond the successful local JAX baseline: convert the actual checkpoint, adapt the exact model/pre/postprocessing contract, compare fixed-noise actions on existing V01 observations, then measure real 3060 memory/latency. No promised fit, FPS or task success.

nvidia_tensorrt_edge_llm.evidence_level: Official experimental export/runtime source inspected; no benchmark for this custom single-wrist Piper checkpoint on RTX 3060 6 GiB was established.
findings: Official experimental pi0.5 export splits visual, prefix, action and cond ONNX components from a converted PyTorch checkpoint; documented examples are FP16.

Supported policy contracts are pi05_libero (state8/action7/horizon10/two cameras), pi05_droid (state8/action8/horizon15/two cameras) and pi05_aloha (state14/action14/horizon50/high camera with optional wrist cameras). None is this project's state7/single-wrist contract.
Matching LIBERO horizon10/action7 is insufficient: this project uses discrete_state_input=True and its own Piper normalization and delta-to-absolute contract.

The token embedding sidecar is not a CPU-resident lookup in the inspected runtime: loadTokenEmbeddings calls loadSafetensors without a device override; its default device is GPU; runtime embeddingLookup is a GPU kernel.
Separating the embedding file from ONNX does not remove its GPU memory. Explicit CPU offload would be an additional implementation.
The support matrix includes x86 Linux developer targets and SM86-capable builds, but does not establish model fit or speed on a 6 GiB 3060.
RTX 3060 is Ampere SM86. Hardware/backend support must be assessed by precision and operator; Blackwell FP4/FP8 results are not evidence for 3060.
ONNX is a graph/weight exchange format; ONNX Runtime CUDA, TensorRT and third-party W4A16 kernels are distinct backends.

A W4A16 RTN weight-only preset need not consume activation calibration data. Other PTQ methods may require representative observations; existing training episodes can supply them while V01 stays held out.
Quantization calibration is unrelated to camera or hand-eye calibration and does not imply retraining the full policy or recapturing the entire dataset.
